h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר נ״ג Pesach — Maamar Nun Gimmel
The Waters as a Wall: Mezuzah, Tefillin and Miriam's Drums at the Sea

p: “And the waters were a wall for them”—
He made them like a kind of wall;
“and on their left”—these are the tefillin.
It did not say “in the merit of the mezuzah
that Yisrael are destined to make.”
that the waters became a wall and a protection,
and through the waters they merited
that the holiness of mezuzah be fixed within them,
For the matter of mezuzah is
מַה שֶׁה' יִתְבָּרֵךְ שׁוֹמֵר עַל הַפֶּתַח
that Hashem, blessed be He, guards the doorway,
“A king of flesh and blood, etc.,
whereas the Holy One, blessed be He—
and He guards them from outside, etc.”
This is like what is said (Shemos 12:23):
“And Hashem will pass over the doorway
and will not allow the destroyer to enter,” etc.
he is the Angel of Death,
he is the evil inclination (Bava Basra 16a).
But then it helped only for that hour.
And the mitzvah of mezuzah is
that they believed that Hashem is One,
they merited the holiness of mezuzah,
and the waters became a wall on their right—
And through the fear they merited
“and on their left—these are the tefillin”:
שֶׁזָּכוּ עַל יְדֵי נֵס הַמַּיִם לְיִרְאָה
through the miracle of the waters they attained fear,
to be a mighty one who conquers his inclination,
like the holiness of the hand-tefillin,
to subjugate the desires and thoughts of our heart
to His service, blessed be His Name.
That is why it did not say
“in the merit of the mezuzah they are destined to make”:
the waters themselves became a wall for them—
on their right the holiness of mezuzah,
and on their left the holiness of tefillin.
For whoever attains faith that Hashem is One,
when it shines in the heart,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן מְשׁוּמָּר מִן הַחֵטְא
“All are reinforcements so that he not sin.”
(Parashah 6, on the verse “And the waters returned”):
“And from where do we know that also against them
the sea was filled with wrath?
As it says, ‘and the waters were a wall (chomah) for them’—
do not read chomah, wall, but cheimah, wrath.
What caused Yisrael to be saved?
‘On their right’—in the merit of the Torah
that they were destined to receive, etc.,
Another interpretation: ‘on their right’—this is the mezuzah
that Yisrael are destined to make,
‘and on their left’—these are the tefillin.”
Now regarding prayer it did not say “destined,”
“And the Children of Yisrael cried out to Hashem.”
But regarding tefillin, why did it not say
On the simple level, one can say
that it relies on the opening clause,
which began with “mezuzah that they are destined to make,”
and this applies to tefillin as well.
why it mentioned the mitzvah of mezuzah
that they were destined to fulfill.
But the matter is as we said:
that then they attained fear and faith,
for one stands before the King,
“If I am a master, where is My fear?”
וּבְכָל מָקוֹם נִדְרָשׁ לְשׁוֹן יִרְאָה עַל תְּפִילָּה
And everywhere the language of fear is expounded as referring to prayer
to be a mighty one who conquers his inclination, as was said.
had not yet been mentioned at all,
שֶׁנֶּאֶמְרָה בְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁמַע וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמוֹעַ
for it is stated in the passages of Shema and Vehayah Im Shamoa
in Mishneh Torah, the Book of Devarim.
That is not so of the mitzvah of tefillin:
אַף שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם כָּל הָאַרְבַּע פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת.
even though they did not yet have all four passages,
nevertheless, since it was said to Moshe
“And it shall be a sign for you on your hand
and a remembrance between your eyes,”
they had already attained the holiness of tefillin.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי בִּמְזוּזָה אָמַר שֶׁעֲתִידִין לַעֲשׂוֹת
Therefore regarding the mezuzah it said “that they are destined to make,”
which is not so of tefillin,
where it did not say “that they are destined to make,”
שֶׁכְּבָר הוֹפִיעַ בָּהֶם קְדוּשַּׁת מִצְוַת תְּפִילִּין
for the holiness of the mitzvah of tefillin had already shone in them
through the word of Hashem, blessed be He,
“And it shall be a sign for you,” etc.
And this is why it mentioned the mitzvah of mezuzah:
for the mitzvah of mezuzah is that one attains
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּטוּחַ מִן הַחֵטְא
and through this one is secure from sin,
and the evil inclination clears out from there.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ לוֹמַר שִׁירָה
And through this they merited to sing the Song,
the Holy Spirit rested upon them
And a maidservant saw at the Sea
that the sea was filled with wrath against them—
against those in whom the faith
was not yet implanted in their heart;
רַק עַל יְדֵי מְזוּזָה שֶׁעֲתִידִין לַעֲשׂוֹת
only through the mezuzah they were destined to make
did they merit the splitting of the Sea.
and sang the Song, as was said.

p: It is further stated in the Mechilta (Shirah):
Had Yisrael said at the Sea,
would ever have ruled over them;
אֶלָּא אָמְרוּ ה' יִמְלוֹךְ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
but they said, ‘Hashem will reign forever and ever’—
And this is the matter of what is written (Shemos 15:20):
“And Miriam the prophetess took the drum.”
“The righteous women of the generation were confident, etc.,
and they took drums out of Egypt.”
And in the Mechilta it says (there):
that the Holy One, blessed be He, would perform for them
and they prepared drums and dances.”
This is difficult: why did the righteous men not go out
with the drums they had prepared?
But regarding the time to come we find
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹשֶׂה מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים וְכוּלֵּי
that the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a dance for the righteous, etc.,
and each one points with his finger, etc.
that after the Exodus from Egypt
they would merit to receive the First Tablets,
for they would not have died (Avodah Zarah 5a),
and there would be freedom from the Angel of Death
and from the evil inclination, which are all one
so they prepared drums and dances
And indeed at the Sea they merited
as one who points with the finger.
אַךְ כֵּיוָן שֶׁזָּרַח בְּפִיהֶם רוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
But once the Holy Spirit shone in their mouths
with “Hashem will reign forever and ever,”
they knew that the time had not yet come,
and that He will reign in the time to come;
so they no longer went out with drums and dances,
for that will be in the future.
But the righteous women of the generation—
that Aharon said, “Remove the golden rings
that are in the ears of your wives”
so that the matter would be delayed,
and in truth the women did not want to give
(as stated in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 45),
“And they removed, etc., that were in their ears,”
and the women did not sin with the Calf—
מִשּׁוּם הָכִי יָצְאוּ כָל הַנָּשִׁים אַחֲרֶיהָ
therefore all the women went out after her
אַף שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְבַּטְּלוּ אֵצֶל הָאֲנָשִׁים
Even though afterwards they were overruled by the men,
for the world is judged by its majority,
and especially women in relation to men,
they went out in dance as in the time to come.
as in “They reel and stagger like a drunkard”
So too Pesach is called the Chag of Matzos:
for once we merit to remove the leaven in the dough,
we dance with drums and dances,
“they reel and stagger like a drunkard.”
For the time of the Chag of Matzos
is to be redeemed at once, completely,
and in Nissan they are destined to be redeemed
and it is the time to attain the dance as in the future,
when each one will point with his finger.
And especially on the last day of Pesach,
the time of the splitting of the Sea,
to point with his finger, “This is my God”—
it is the time to merit redemption

Rabbi Yosi: Israel accepted the Torah only so that the Angel of Death should not rule over them. Rashi: for they would have lived forever.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Shevi'i shel Pesach 25 — “‘Hashem will reign forever and ever’: with this Hashem sealed upon Israel that forever and ever they will be called servants of Hashem, and even if they enter further subjugation and many concealments, the heart of Israel will no longer be under subjugation. When Hashem sealed that He will reign over Israel forever and ever, this freedom was fixed in Israel, and holiness was so fixed in Israel that it is said, ‘And Miriam the prophetess took the drum in her hand’: this hints that these words of Torah were so fixed in Israel that they spread even to the women.” Connection: Both join ‘Hashem will reign forever and ever’ to Miriam’s drum; where Pri Tzaddik reads the future tense as postponement that halted the men, Sod Yesharim reads it as a seal of inner freedom that reached even the women.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Chamishah Asar B'Av 4 — “At the Splitting of the Sea it is said, ‘And Miriam the prophetess took the drum in her hand, and all the women went out after her with drums and dances.’ These two instruments subdue the two husks: the drum subdues Lilis, the husk of sadness and wailing, and the dance subdues Machalas, the husk of revelry and levity. At the Sea there was a revelation of the surrounding light for that hour, for the Splitting of the Sea depends on Atika; therefore the women too, whose minds are light, could go out with drum and dance, for in the revealing of the surrounding light there is no distinction of levels.” Connection: Both ask why the women went out in dance at the Sea; there it rests on the surrounding light, which has no levels, and on drum and dance subduing two husks.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Kalonymus Kalman Epstein, Maor VaShemesh, Beshalach — “The Gemara says that the Holy One, blessed be He, will in the future make a dance for the righteous, and each one will point with his finger. In the future all will attain the light of His Godliness equally, like a circle that has no head or end, like the dance of the vineyard whose center is equally near to the whole circle. This was the intent of Miriam the prophetess, who brought all the women out after her and circled with them, to draw down the supernal light. Therefore Moshe said ‘I will sing,’ in the future tense, because the full light had not yet appeared; but Miriam drew down that light through her circling, and so she said ‘Sing’ now.” Connection: The Maor VaShemesh reads the women’s dance at the Sea as an early taste of the future dance while the men’s song looked ahead; he adds the circle as the form of equal attainment.
